To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RevErb α antagonizes the transactivational activity of PPAR α on the HD- PPRE.
RevErbalpha antagonizes transactivation from the HD-PPRERE by inhibiting PPARalpha/RXRalpha-dependent transactivation.
RevErbalpha antagonizes PPARalpha-dependent transactivation of HD-PPRE reporter gene constructs in a response element specific manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which nuclear receptors modulate gene expression.
the role of RevErbα as an orphan nuclear hormone receptor that can modulate the activity of the PPARα-RXRα heterodimer on the PPRE of the HD gene.
the identification and characterization of RevErbα target genes and its role in metabolic homeostatic pathways.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RevErb is able to modulate the expression from the PPREs of the HD and AOx genes by antagonizing PPARα/Rxrα-dependent transactivation.
the RevErb family member RevErbα acts as a transcriptional repressor in a response element specific manner by inhibiting PPARα/RXα-dependent transactivation.
the RevErb α protein binds to the PPRE in the promoter of the hydratase/dehydrogenase gene and inhibits the transcriptional activation of this gene by PPAR α.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RevErb α can bind to a response element in the promoter of the hydratase-dehydrogenease gene (HD) but not the fatty acyl-Coa oxidase gene (AOX).
the orphan nuclear receptor RevErbα inhibits PPARα/RXRA-dependent transactivation from the PPRE in the promoter of the HD gene by binding to the HD-PPRER.
we have shown Rev-erbs are capable of antagonizing PPARα activity and that they are capable of antagonism in a response element specific manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
orphan nuclear hormone receptors can modulate the activity of other nuclear hormone receptors in a response element specific manner.
RevErb is a novel regulator of peroxisomal gene expression and that it can inhibit the activity of the peroxiome proliferator-activator receptor (PPAR).

RevErbalpha, an orphan nuclear hormone receptor (i.e. a receptor for which the ligand is not known) modulates the expression of a gene involved in peroxisome β-oxidation by binding to a response element in the upstream region of the gene.
